newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast power prices soften on mild weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast power prices soften on mild weather.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the southeastern U.S. remained soft Thursday, still pressured by mild temperatures in the region and in surrounding areas, sources said.
"Temperatures are milder, and prices are down," one market source said, noting the weak demand was keeping many traders away from the market.

Firm, peak power prices in the northern part of the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) territory for Friday were mostly lower in the $14.00-15.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), down from Wednesday's $15.50-16.50 trading range.
Next week's peak prices into TVA were talked notionally in the $19.00-20.00 range.
Firm, off-peak electricity in northern TVA was assessed around $9.00, down sharply from Wednesday's $12.50 level.
At the Georgia/Florida border, prices for firm, peak electricity in 16 hour blocks for Friday delivery were fairly steady in the $22.00-23.00 per MWh range.
Next week's peak prices at the border were talked in the $23.00-24.00 range.
Firm, off-peak power for Friday at the Ga./Fla. border was notionally assessed at $14.50-16.00.
In Florida, where most daytime highs are in the 70s Fahrenheit and lows are in the 50s, peak power prices on a 16-hour schedule were talked again in the $23.00-24.00 area.
Off-peak power prices in Florida hovered in the $16.00-17.00 area, traders said.
Temperatures in the Southeast are expected to remain above-normal Friday but then fall to normal to slightly below-normal levels this weekend.
Most sources said they are not expecting a significant rebound in prices as a result as many buyers will likely rely on coal and hydro supplies instead to meet the marginal rise in demand.
Separately, Southern Co's 822 megawatt Farley 2 nuclear power unit in Dothan, Ala., is scheduled to restart on December 15 after being shut October 12 for refueling and maintenance.
